title: the suite's anti-vacuity floors hardcode counts: tests compare what they read against numbers written into them, and some state today's totals in their failure text
body:
Found by vc on 2026-10-23 while reviewing 0203's documentation.bats arm, two arms below a floor of this kind.

hv's rule, in the user-scope AGENTS.md every session loads: "Never hardcode a count. No number of checks, tests, liberators or anything else goes into a doc, a guard, a test or a constant in code ... A count already written down is deleted, never corrected." devbin's suite carries counts of this kind. Each was added for a good reason, so that a scan or an extractor that read nothing could not pass over an empty set (LESSONS: a broken instrument that returns zero is never re-run). But each compares what the test read against a number written into the test. Each goes stale as the tree grows, and some go wrong at once:

- An exact count: dispatch.bats:2111 (`[ "$rows" -eq 29 ]`, the size of the arm's own fixture table, written out a second time).
- Floors that name today's total in their failure text, which is wrong as soon as a page or command is added: help.bats:1140, :1155 and :1426 ("devbin ships 28").
- Floors: contract.bats:614, :783, :861, :985 and :1251; documentation.bats:282, :599 and :818; infra-profile.bats:1220; install.bats:968; neutral.bats:274, :419 and :420; vendoredmd.bats:122.
- Comments that state a current count: vendoredmd.bats:121, and help.bats' "at least today's 28" above :1140. A comment recording a past measurement, such as 0112 closing on 16 of 28, is history and stays.

Not counts, and out of scope: exit statuses (clean.bats' 124), signal thresholds (runlog.bats' 128) and a pipe buffer's size (review.bats' 65536).

**Fix.** Each floor keeps its purpose without a number:
- Compare against a referent read at run time, eg the extractor finds every command `builtin_commands` lists, or every page `lib/pages/*.md` holds.
- Where only presence is at stake, check that the scan read at least one file.
- Where a floor was kept because a comparison cannot see a deletion that both sides lose (help.bats:1150-1155), name the arm that does see it (every built-in has a page), or add one.
- An exact count of a fixture is computed from the fixture.
- Every count in failure text and comments that describes the tree as it is now is deleted.

The arms change, but what they protect does not, so no new arm is added.

Done when: no test under tests/ compares a number it measured against a count written into it, nor states a current count in its text, apart from the protocol constants above; each floor's purpose is held by a referent, a presence check or a named arm; the files touched pass under BSD and GNU tools; and the fix has landed in the next batch release.

## Resolution

Fixed at 5460ac09 in the 0.1.13 batch, on landing suite 20261023-2029 at 23f5f70e (2435 of 2435 ok, 5 skips, seal empty) (dc built it on 0205's tip, 15e7edf8, as two kinds read apart, each with its critic fold; vc landed it).

- Every vacuity guard keeps its purpose without a number, as one of these:
  - a presence check, where completeness is another arm's;
  - a referent read at run time: docs/configuration.md's documented paths for the schema key extractor, git's tracked files for check-attr and the lint gate, a find over lib/pages for the page scan, the pages and template for the prettier run, second greps for dispatch's split-args sites, raw array runs and boolean readers, devbin's own handlers for the help listing, the tables and lists dispatch's loops read, the shipped db options through fixture_catalogue_count, and the release core's own step table;
  - the named check that sees a deletion: every built-in's page.
- install.bats's control find reads its own status. The identifier charset is held inside is_identifier.
- Every count of an arm's own fixture is computed from the fixture: a probe directory, a plant file, an array the fixture is built from, a list the fixture records, or the input the arm passes. A unit's expected words are compared whole. Each computed control also checks it planted something.
- The literals left are each ruled: counts only the code under test can derive (YAML tallies, parser- and analysis-derived counts), and design constants. Both widen the Done when's one exception, the protocol constants.
  - Each such count is the code under test's answer over the arm's own fixture, never a count of the tree, and computing it in the test would re-implement that code. vc ruled each site on 2026-10-23, from the list in dc's HANDOVER: the options an arm's YAML declares that the dispatcher ran, skipped or found inactive; the log keys an arm's YAML gives doctor; the gates and sidecars a YAML fixture declares; the tests dormancy counts in a cargo listing; the DMARC records parsed from the XML fixtures, through the report too; the assertions the infra checker derives from the arm's profile; which trees clean's walk counts; which installs fall outside fleet's audit frame; the ancestry the installer records; nonempty_lines' answer on a literal input; the checks doctor fails; what upgrade counts as skipped; and the placeholders render counts.
  - The design constants left: dormancy's two legs, a file linted again alone exactly once, a table's header and separator, the runner's two lanes and the serial lane's one job, a block's begin and end markers, and one changed line as two diff lines.
- Every comment or failure text that stated the size of something the tree grows lost the number. Records of past measurements stay.
- No new arm. Every touched suite, the tree scans and help pass under BSD and GNU tools.
